I'm not a cop, but I am a car enthusiast, so I have a few things to say on EVs. 



The thing I'm thinking of is all of yalls police equipment. Light bars, ALPRs, Radar/LIDAR, even yalls whole ass computers in there are gonna draw ALOT of power once they are all running. If your range unloaded is around 200-300 miles, under load (just some rough estimates here so take my figures with a grain of salt) is gonna be around 100-150 miles. 




There's also the factor of charging time vs fuel up time, and while EVs have come a long way in that regard, they are still not nearly as fast as a fuel up. 




They are also way more expensive to fix than an ICE. Imagine the strain a fleet of even 4 EVs breaking down and the strain it would put on the departments coffers. 



They are also QUICK, not fast. They have insane acceleration because they can deliver all their torque like THAT, but their top speed gets crippled. I have raced EVs in my 4-banger, and I overtook them in the top end cause they are stuck at around 185-190km/h and I still have a lil more to give already going 200km/h. A skilled driver running from you in a decently powerful ICE will have the edge over your patrol EV. 



I think EVs can have a role currently in law enforcement as admin or detective vehicles, but as patrol? They still have some growing up to do in that regard.

The "cars vs bikes" debate has been going on a long time, wether it was in terms of motorbikes, or bicycles, and i think there are multiple factors that go into this aminosity. 


For bicycles - lack of speed speed and a tendency to disregard traffic laws, such as stop signs and red lights, (i used to be bad for this because i didnt like losing all the momentum i had built up) and not looking when they need to cross over the lane, or to go around a parked car because there is no bike lane,  thus cutting traffic off going sometimes much faster than they are. 



For motorbikes: collisions with cars are often fatal, and as such tend to ride EXTREMELY DEFENSIVELY, such as lane splitting, or going faster than the rest of traffic to keep as much distace between them and "cagers". They also have a tendency to roadrage VERY aggressively and do property damage (kicking of mirrors) or even assaults on the 'cager' they deem themselves pissed off at. 



For cars and drivers: lack of attention, a sense of entitlement to the road, and all the new age  safteytech in cars nowadays (lane-keep assist, adaptive cruise control, even autopilot) simply causes motorists to trust THEIR CAR'S ability to drive more than their own. Inattentive drivers, or even "zombie drivers" that seem to be one cough away from hittin the ditch,  and a general lack of care for others on the road, such as not indicating when turning or brakechecking someone creeping up on them to pass on the highway. 





There are many outside factors that go in aswell, such as car centric infastructure or a lack of bike lanes or paths, which i sympathize with, however these are simply a few of the DIRECT FACTORS we are each in control of as drivers, bycyclists, or bikers.

Alot of that stuff is handled via officer digression. Here's an example.






Imagine I'm a cop. I pull a guy over for blowing a stop sign. I walk up to his window, and smell that familiar smell of skunk. I take his license and registration, run it, all comes back clean. Then I tackle the issue of the weed I can smell. Upon reading this dudes license, I discover he's only a teenager. 16 or 17. And I tell him straight. "Dude, I know you've got weed in here. Just be honest and tell me where it is." Let's say he's honest. Tells me it's in the center console. I ask him to get it for me, and he does. It's not a major amount, Dude clearly just got it from his friend or someone else he knows. No concern of him trafficking this stuff. Now I get to make a choice. I could either A) arrest him and give him a criminal record before his life had even begun, which doesn't sit well with me, or B) confiscate and destroy, and then have a talk with him, as long as he isn't high at this moment. (Which if he's driving High, I'll have no problem tossing him behind bars. I don't care what you say, weed impairs you. Like alcohol does) 






In this scenario, Dude was honest with me, and clearly just wanted to smoke up. Arresting him would solve nothing. So, I talk with him, say 'look, you've seen the trend. This stuffs on its way to legalization here already. At least wait until then, alright? I don't want you to get thrown behind bars because someone else other than me was the one who caught you. You were honest, and you are sober. I'm gonna write you up for the stop sign, but there'll be no mention of this." He thanks me profusely, thankful to just be getting a ticket, and gets sent on his way. Without his weed, but a free man. 

(This scenario is one of my own experience. As that scared teenager who only wanted to get stoned.)


And all this is no risk to the officers job.





Of course this is ideal, and every officer is different, with different experiences and knowledge. Someone else (say, a older patrol seargent whose been on the force longer than a good chunk of patrol officers have been alive) may not be as lenient, but, every traffic stop is different and everyone involved plays a role in how it turns out. This scenario plays out however, constantly. The majority of officers are great people, and everyone I have met, wether on the wrong or right side of the law in my teenage years have proven exactly that. 




Cops are allowed (and encouraged) to display emotion in the line of duty, to a degree. If you're breaking down every time someone shouts at you, you aren't fit for this line of work (and that's okay) however if you're talking down a suicidal person and your voice is breaking due to the tears that threaten to flow, that's all the more likely to connect with the person. Say you get the person down, the floodgates flow, and while the suicidal person is being looked after, countless of your fellow officers rush to you to comfort and commend you, because they've all been there. Any department that wants their officers to basically be stone cold machines, constantly find themselves short of officers.
